definitions.gloss: to envision, to picture in one's mind, to imagine
definitions.explanation: To form a mental image of something, especially a future scenario, an ideal, or a scene. Implies a vivid and often positive or hopeful visualization.

examples.japanese: {理想|りそう}の{未来|みらい}を{思|おも}い{描|えが}く。
{子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}{思|おも}い{描|えが}いていた{大人|おとな}の{姿|すがた}とは{違|ちが}った。
examples.english: It was different from the image of adulthood I had envisioned as a child.

examples.japanese: {成功|せいこう}した{自分|じぶん}の{姿|すがた}を{思|おも}い{描|えが}きながら、{毎日|まいにち}{努力|どりょく}を{続|つづ}けている。
examples.english: Picturing myself as a success, I keep working hard every day.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound verb combining {思|おも}う (to think) and {描|えが}く (to draw, to depict). Emphasizes the visual, imaginative quality of the thought — not just thinking about something but actively visualizing it. Often used with {未来|みらい} (future), {理想|りそう} (ideal), or {姿|すがた} (image, figure).

COMMON PATTERNS:
Godan verb ending in く. The object is marked with を: Xを{思|おも}い{描|えが}く.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {未来|みらい}を{思|おも}い{描|えが}く: to envision the future
- {理想|りそう}を{思|おも}い{描|えが}く: to picture an ideal
- {姿|すがた}を{思|おも}い{描|えが}く: to envision a figure/image
- {夢|ゆめ}を{思|おも}い{描|えが}く: to picture a dream
